set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 30-year-old woman has erythema nodosum, bilateral ankle arthritis and hilar lymphadenopathy on chest radiograph. Which is the most likely underlying diagnosis?
opts: Primary tuberculosis with mediastinal involvement
Tuberculosis is a trigger and can produce hilar changes, but the triad here is characteristic of Löfgren.
Streptococcal infection with post-infectious reaction
Streptococcus is the commonest infectious trigger but does not cause hilar lymphadenopathy.
Sarcoidosis presenting as Löfgren syndrome
Correct, and it has the best prognosis of all sarcoidosis presentations, with over 90% spontaneous remission.
Inflammatory bowel disease, most likely Crohn's disease
Bowel disease is an association but would not produce hilar lymphadenopathy.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 19-year-old man reports excessive sweating of both palms and soles since early adolescence, enough to smudge his handwriting. It never occurs while he is asleep. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Primary focal hyperhidrosis
Correct — bilateral, focal, adolescent onset and absent during sleep are the defining features.
Secondary generalised hyperhidrosis
That is generalised, may be asymmetric, and can occur at night.
Frey syndrome producing gustatory sweating
That causes unilateral facial sweating triggered by eating.
Autonomic neuropathy from undiagnosed diabetes
That is asymmetric with associated neurologic features.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 68-year-old man has several uniformly tan, well-demarcated macules 5 to 12 mm across on the dorsal hands and forearms, with no scale or induration. Dermoscopy shows finger-like projections and a moth-eaten border. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Solar lentigo
Correct — uniform pigment on chronically exposed skin with those dermoscopic features.
Lentigo maligna
That is asymmetric with irregular border and structureless pigment on dermoscopy.
Seborrheic keratosis
That is stuck-on with comedone-like openings on dermoscopy.
Pigmented actinic keratosis
That has a rough scaly texture rather than a smooth macular surface.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 28-year-old woman develops itchy 3 mm red papules on her chest and forearms hours after the first sunny weekend of spring. The same thing happened last April and settled by midsummer. Her face is spared. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus
That is distinguished by antinuclear and anti-Ro antibodies and does not harden.
Solar urticaria of the chest and forearms
That produces wheals within minutes that resolve within an hour.
Erythropoietic protoporphyria of adult onset
That begins in childhood with burning pain and raised red-cell protoporphyrin.
Polymorphous light eruption
Correct — spring onset, sparing of chronically exposed skin, and summer hardening are all characteristic.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 31-year-old man returns from a beach holiday with painful blisters followed by odd streaked brown marks on both forearms. He had been squeezing limes into drinks in the sun. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Berloque dermatitis from bergapten in a fragrance product
That produces a drip pattern on the neck and décolletage.
Chronic actinic dermatitis of the forearms and dorsal hands
That is a persistent eczematous eruption in older males.
Allergic contact dermatitis to an ingredient in his sunscreen
That would be eczematous and would not follow a streaked pattern.
Phytophotodermatitis from furanocoumarins in lime juice
Correct — linear streaked hyperpigmentation after lime plus sun is the classic presentation.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 34-year-old man reports months of intensely itchy, burning bumps on his elbows, knees and buttocks. Examination shows grouped papules and excoriations symmetrically distributed, with few intact vesicles. He has no gastrointestinal complaints. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Atopic dermatitis of adult onset
That favours a flexural distribution with raised immunoglobulin E and no immunoglobulin A deposition.
Linear immunoglobulin A bullous dermatosis
That shows linear rather than granular immunoglobulin A at the basement membrane.
Dermatitis herpetiformis
Correct — the symmetric extensor distribution with burning that precedes lesions, and gastrointestinal symptoms may be absent despite villous atrophy.
Scabies infestation of the trunk and extremities
That would show burrows in the web spaces and a positive skin scraping.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 44-year-old woman has itchy wheals that persist for two to three days and fade leaving brownish discoloration. Which is the most appropriate next step?
opts: Skin biopsy, since lesions persisting beyond twenty-four hours suggest urticarial vasculitis
Correct — the persistence and residual bruising are what take this out of simple urticaria.
Increase the second-generation antihistamine to four times the standard licensed daily dose
Dose escalation is right for chronic urticaria but not before this atypical pattern is explained.
Measure complement C4 and C1-esterase inhibitor level and function
That is indicated for recurrent angio-oedema occurring without wheals.
Begin omalizumab at 300 mg subcutaneously every four weeks
That is reserved for refractory chronic urticaria after a diagnosis is established.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 59-year-old woman wants treatment for photoaging of her face. Which topical agent is the only one approved by the Food and Drug Administration for this indication?
opts: Niacinamide applied twice daily
It is anti-inflammatory and reduces sallowness but is not approved.
Tretinoin at 0.025 to 0.1%
Correct — it stimulates collagen and inhibits matrix metalloproteinases, over six to twelve months.
Vitamin C at 10 to 20%
It neutralises reactive oxygen species but is not approved for photoaging.
Hydroquinone at 2 to 4%
That treats hyperpigmentation rather than photoaging as a whole.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 24-year-old woman spent six hours at the beach. Eight hours later her shoulders are red, hot and tender, without blisters. Which is the most appropriate management?
opts: A short course of oral corticosteroids tapered over the following week
Systemic steroids are not part of the management of ordinary sunburn.
Cold water immersion with ice packs applied directly to the erythema
Cool rather than cold water is advised, and ice risks further injury.
Topical silver sulfadiazine applied twice daily under an occlusive layer
That is a burn dressing agent and is not used for first-degree sunburn.
Cool compresses, oral hydration and an early nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug
Correct — early nonsteroidals reduce the prostaglandin-mediated inflammation and pain.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 29-year-old woman has had chronic spontaneous urticaria for eight months and asks whether it will ever settle. Which is the most appropriate counselling point?
opts: Complete avoidance of all common food allergens will resolve the condition
Dietary avoidance does not address idiopathic or autoimmune chronic urticaria.
About half of chronic urticaria resolves spontaneously within a year, and over half of cases have no identifiable trigger
Correct — this reframes the search for a cause that often does not exist.
A specific environmental or dietary trigger can be identified in almost every case if enough testing is done
More than half of chronic urticaria is idiopathic.
The condition is lifelong once it has persisted beyond six weeks in duration
Spontaneous resolution occurs in about half within a year.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 33-year-old man has recurrent episodes of lip and periorbital swelling without any wheals. Which is the most appropriate initial testing?
opts: Serum tryptase with a search for Darier's sign on examination
That combination investigates mastocytosis.
Autologous serum skin test for autoimmune chronic urticaria
That is used in chronic urticaria with wheals.
Thyroid-stimulating hormone with anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies
Those form part of the chronic urticaria workup rather than isolated angio-oedema.
Complement C4 with C1-esterase inhibitor level and function
Correct — angio-oedema without wheals should raise hereditary angio-oedema.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 38-year-old man with newly confirmed dermatitis herpetiformis is about to start dapsone. Which is the most appropriate next step?
opts: Check glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase status before the first dose
Correct, then monitor the blood count for haemolytic anaemia and methaemoglobinaemia.
Check thyroid-stimulating hormone and anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies
Autoimmune thyroid disease is an association but not the pre-dapsone safety check.
Arrange small bowel biopsy before any treatment is commenced
Gastroenterology evaluation matters but does not gate starting dapsone.
Perform HLA-DQ2 and HLA-DQ8 typing to confirm susceptibility
Typing is used when serology is equivocal rather than before dapsone.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 52-year-old man is admitted with Stevens-Johnson syndrome six days after starting trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Which is the single most important initial action?
opts: Begin high-dose systemic corticosteroids and continue for several weeks
Steroids remain controversial and are avoided where infection is active.
Apply silver sulfadiazine dressings to the areas of detached epidermis
Silver sulfadiazine is specifically avoided because of sulfonamide cross-reaction.
Discontinue the suspected drug and every other non-essential medication
Correct — earlier withdrawal is strongly associated with improved survival, and each day of delay worsens it.
Begin intravenous immunoglobulin at one gram per kilogram for three days
Immunomodulation follows, but drug withdrawal is the action that changes survival.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 54-year-old man reports new generalised sweating including at night, with episodes of headache and palpitations, and his blood pressure is 178/104. Which is the most appropriate initial testing?
opts: Minor's starch-iodine test to map the distribution of sweating
That maps primary focal disease rather than investigating a secondary cause.
Gravimetric measurement of axillary sweat output over five minutes
That quantifies sweating rather than identifying the underlying cause.
Photopatch testing to a standard series of photoallergens
That investigates photoallergic contact dermatitis.
Twenty-four hour urine metanephrines and catecholamines
Correct — episodic sweating with headache, palpitations and hypertension points to phaeochromocytoma.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 31-year-old woman has her fourth episode of target lesions on the hands in eighteen months. Each episode has followed an oral herpes outbreak. Which is the most appropriate long-term management?
opts: Dapsone titrated to response with regular blood count monitoring
Right drug, wrong indication: dapsone is for refractory recurrent disease that is not herpes-associated.
Hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice daily taken continuously
Also reserved for refractory recurrent disease without a herpes trigger.
Acyclovir 400 mg five times daily during each acute episode only
Treating episodes does not prevent them; suppression is what reduces recurrence.
Suppressive acyclovir 400 mg twice daily or valacyclovir 500 mg daily
Correct — recurrent disease is strongly associated with recurrent herpes simplex, and suppression is the answer.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A patient with pyoderma gangrenosum asks why the wound clinic will not debride the ulcer as they would for other wounds. Which is the most appropriate explanation?
opts: Debridement is deferred only until systemic immunosuppression has taken effect
Debridement is avoided altogether because of pathergy.
The ulcer worsens with trauma, a phenomenon called pathergy, so debridement makes it larger
Correct — this is the single most consequential management point in the condition.
The ulcer is infected and debridement would spread bacteria into the bloodstream
The condition is not infectious despite its name.
The ulcer will heal faster if left completely undisturbed by any dressing
Moist wound dressings and non-adherent contact layers are actively used.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 55-year-old kidney transplant recipient asks why she is being seen so often for skin checks. Which is the most appropriate counselling point?
opts: Frequent review is a routine protocol requirement rather than a clinical necessity
The elevated risk is the clinical reason for the increased surveillance.
Skin cancers in transplant recipients behave less aggressively than in other patients
They are both more frequent and more aggressive in this group.
Immunosuppression raises the risk of actinic keratosis and skin cancer about sixty-fold
Correct — transplant recipients need aggressive photoprotection and biannual skin surveillance.
Transplant medication makes the skin more sensitive to burning within minutes of sun
The concern is cumulative carcinogenic risk rather than acute burning.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: The parent of a child with a single asymptomatic granuloma annulare ring asks whether treatment is needed. Which is the most appropriate counselling point?
opts: It is benign and self-limiting, with about half resolving within two years, so treatment is for cosmesis or discomfort
Correct, and there is no malignant potential.
It is premalignant and should be excised to prevent later transformation
There is no malignant potential in granuloma annulare.
It is contagious to other children and school attendance should be limited
The condition is not infectious.
It will persist unchanged for life unless systemic immunosuppressive therapy is started early in the course
About half resolve spontaneously within two years.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 25-year-old man with erythema nodosum has no bowel or respiratory symptoms and no recent drug exposure. Which initial investigations should be ordered?
opts: Complement C4, C1-esterase inhibitor function and serum tryptase
That panel investigates urticaria and angio-oedema.
Fasting insulin, haemoglobin A1c and a full lipid profile
That panel investigates acanthosis nigricans.
Antistreptolysin O titre, throat culture, chest radiograph and inflammatory markers
Correct, with tuberculin or interferon gamma testing and a pregnancy test where relevant.
Serum protein electrophoresis, antinuclear and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies
That panel investigates pyoderma gangrenosum.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: An infant has generalised blistering from minimal trauma and the subtype is unclear. Which test determines the level of cleavage?
opts: Skin biopsy with transmission electron microscopy
Correct — the gold standard, with immunofluorescence antigen mapping localising the missing protein.
Skin biopsy with direct immunofluorescence for immunoglobulin G
That identifies acquired autoimmune blistering rather than mapping an inherited cleavage plane.
Serum enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay for structural antibodies
Inherited epidermolysis bullosa is not antibody-mediated.
Bacterial culture of blister fluid with sensitivity testing
Culture addresses secondary infection rather than the diagnosis.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 15-year-old with a body mass index in the 97th percentile has velvety, darkened, thickened skin at the back of the neck and in both axillae. Which is the most appropriate initial testing?
opts: Fasting glucose, haemoglobin A1c, fasting insulin and a lipid panel
Correct — the finding is a visible marker of insulin resistance and warrants metabolic assessment.
Computed tomography of chest, abdomen and pelvis with upper endoscopy
That workup is reserved for suspected malignant acanthosis nigricans.
Potassium hydroxide preparation of scrapings from the affected skin
That would investigate tinea versicolor, one of the differentials.
Skin biopsy of the posterior neck for histological confirmation
Biopsy is rarely needed since the diagnosis is primarily clinical.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 28-year-old woman is recovering from carbamazepine-induced Stevens-Johnson syndrome and is being discharged. Which is the most appropriate counselling point?
opts: Avoid the causative drug for six months, after which a cautious supervised rechallenge in hospital is reasonable to consider
Rechallenge is never appropriate; avoidance is lifelong.
Expect complete recovery within weeks, with no need for any specialist follow-up after discharge
Long-term ophthalmology, dermatology and psychological follow-up are all expected.
Avoid sun exposure and use broad-spectrum sunscreen daily to prevent the eruption from recurring
The reaction is drug-triggered rather than light-triggered.
Avoid the causative drug class for life, wear a medical alert bracelet, and have first-degree relatives counselled on shared genetic risk
Correct — the human leukocyte antigen association makes family counselling part of the discharge advice.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 44-year-old woman has an itchy, eczematous eruption on sun-exposed skin that extends onto covered areas, beginning after two weeks of a new sunscreen. Which test establishes the diagnosis?
opts: Antinuclear antibody panel including anti-Ro and anti-La antibodies
That screens for lupus rather than confirming a photoallergy.
Photopatch testing with duplicate sets, one of which is irradiated
Correct — it is the gold standard for photoallergy; a reaction only on the irradiated set confirms it.
Minimal erythema dose testing to ultraviolet A and ultraviolet B
That quantifies light sensitivity but does not identify the responsible chemical.
Skin biopsy of the eruption sent for direct immunofluorescence
Biopsy is rarely needed and immunofluorescence addresses other diseases.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 41-year-old woman with painful skin and oral erosions has suspected Stevens-Johnson syndrome. Which diagnostic test is considered pathognomonic?
opts: Transmission electron microscopy with immunofluorescence antigen mapping
That is the gold standard for epidermolysis bullosa.
Serum tryptase measured within four hours of the acute eruption
That is used in the evaluation of mast cell disease and anaphylaxis.
Punch biopsy showing full-thickness epidermal necrosis with junctional separation
Correct — that histology is the pathognomonic finding named for this condition.
Direct immunofluorescence showing granular immunoglobulin A at the papillae
That finding establishes dermatitis herpetiformis.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 24-year-old woman with primary hyperhidrosis says she has been told repeatedly that she just needs to wash more and relax. Which is the most appropriate counselling point?
opts: Primary hyperhidrosis is a medical condition rather than a problem of hygiene or anxiety
Correct — the misconception is addressed directly, and quality-of-life impairment is comparable to severe psoriasis.
Improved hygiene and stress reduction will resolve the sweating over time
Anxiety exacerbates the condition but neither causes nor cures it.
The condition affects a very small minority and treatment options are limited
It affects roughly 3 to 5% of the population and has a full treatment ladder.
Sweating of this kind always indicates a serious underlying systemic illness
Primary disease is idiopathic; secondary causes are what require investigation.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 49-year-old man with toxic epidermal necrolysis has been admitted to the burn unit and the offending drug stopped. Which pharmacologic therapy has the strongest current evidence base?
opts: Subcutaneous omalizumab given every four weeks
That is a therapy for refractory chronic urticaria.
Cyclosporine at 3 to 5 mg/kg daily, started early
Correct — early initiation is preferred and the evidence is the strongest of the available options.
Prophylactic broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics
Antibiotic prophylaxis is specifically not recommended; treat confirmed infection.
Pulsed methylprednisolone continued for fourteen days
Systemic corticosteroids remain controversial in this setting.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 12-year-old with recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa attends for review. Which surveillance should now begin?
opts: Annual bone densitometry to monitor for treatment-related osteoporosis
This is not among the described surveillance requirements.
Annual squamous cell carcinoma surveillance, which starts after the age of ten
Correct — the severe scarring of dystrophic disease carries a substantial carcinoma risk.
Annual colonoscopy to detect gastrointestinal involvement of the disease
Endoscopy is performed if oesophageal stricture is suspected rather than for surveillance.
Annual echocardiography to monitor for the development of cardiomyopathy
This is not among the described surveillance requirements.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 71-year-old woman with toxic epidermal necrolysis has a SCORTEN of 5 on admission. Beyond intensive care, which referral is specifically indicated at this score?
opts: Physical therapy, for early prevention of joint contracture
Rehabilitation matters in survivors but is not what the score triggers.
Plastic surgery, for planning of definitive skin grafting
Wound care uses biological dressings rather than early grafting.
Palliative care, for an early goals-of-care discussion
Correct — a score of five or above carries a predicted mortality near 90% and palliative involvement is named.
Genetics, for human leukocyte antigen haplotype testing
That is appropriate later, and for at-risk populations rather than at this score.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 49-year-old man with rosacea reports gritty, red eyes and blurred vision that has worsened over two weeks. Which is the most appropriate next step?
opts: Advise artificial tears and reassess at his next routine appointment
Visual change with corneal risk should not wait for routine review.
Urgent ophthalmology referral for slit-lamp examination
Correct — ocular rosacea with visual symptoms risks corneal scarring if untreated.
Begin topical ivermectin to the face and review in six weeks
That addresses cutaneous disease and would delay assessment of the eye.
Begin sub-antimicrobial doxycycline and review in three months
Doxycycline is used in ocular rosacea, but visual symptoms need urgent assessment first.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: A 61-year-old man with no obesity develops widespread velvety hyperpigmentation over eight weeks, involving the axillae, the oral mucosa and the palms, which have a thickened rugose appearance. Which is the most appropriate next step?
opts: Reassure her that the change is cosmetic and arrange routine follow-up with lifestyle advice in six months
The tempo and distribution here demand urgent evaluation rather than reassurance.
Urgent evaluation for an underlying malignancy, particularly of the gastrointestinal tract
Correct — rapid onset, extensive involvement, mucosal change and tripe palms indicate malignant acanthosis nigricans.
Begin metformin to reduce insulin resistance and reassess in three months
That addresses the benign insulin-resistant form, which this presentation is not.
Begin topical retinoids for cosmetic improvement of the affected areas
Cosmetic treatment would delay the necessary malignancy workup.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 27-year-old woman has tender red lumps on both shins that appeared over a week, preceded by fever and joint aches. Examination shows bilateral tender nodules 2 to 4 cm on the anterior tibial surfaces; none is ulcerated. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Erythema nodosum
Correct — bilateral tender anterior shin nodules that do not ulcerate, after a prodrome of fever and arthralgia.
Nodular vasculitis, also called erythema induratum
That favours the posterior legs, ulcerates, and shows lobular panniculitis on biopsy.
Cellulitis of both lower legs
Cellulitis is unilateral, warm and expanding, with positive cultures and antibiotic response.
Superficial thrombophlebitis of the long saphenous vein
That produces a linear cord along the vein and is confirmed on ultrasound.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 72-year-old outdoor worker has rough, scaly, erythematous papules with a sandpaper texture scattered across his balding scalp and dorsal hands. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Seborrheic keratosis
That is stuck-on and waxy without the gritty sandpaper feel.
Bowen disease
That is a well-demarcated scaly plaque rather than multiple gritty papules.
Scalp psoriasis
That produces thick silvery plaques with a different distribution.
Actinic keratosis
Correct — sandpaper texture on chronically sun-exposed skin, the commonest precancerous lesion worldwide.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 34-year-old man started lamotrigine three weeks ago. He has three days of fever and sore throat, then painful dusky macules on the trunk, erosions of the lips and conjunctivae, and epidermal detachment over about 6% of his body surface. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Erythema multiforme major
That is usually herpes-associated with acral targets and less mucosal disease.
Stevens-Johnson syndrome
Correct — detachment under 10% with mucosal involvement, three weeks into an aromatic anticonvulsant.
Toxic epidermal necrolysis
That requires detachment above 30% of the body surface area.
Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome
That is toxin-mediated and spares the mucous membranes entirely.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A neonate develops blisters over the hands and feet after routine handling and nappy changes. There is no fever and the mother is well. Family history includes a father with similar childhood blistering that healed without scars. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Junctional epidermolysis bullosa of the Herlitz subtype
That is generalised with poor wound healing, nail dystrophy and the highest mortality.
Bullous pemphigoid of the neonatal period
Bullous pemphigoid is an acquired autoimmune disease of older adults.
Epidermolysis bullosa simplex
Correct — localised to palms and soles, healing without scarring, and autosomal dominant.
Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome
That is infectious and toxin-mediated, and would present with fever.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 28-year-old man has a two-day history of a rash on his hands and forearms. Examination shows symmetric lesions on the palms and dorsal hands, each with a dusky centre, a pale swollen ring and an outer red halo. He had a cold sore ten days ago. There is no mucosal involvement. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Secondary syphilis involving the palms and soles
This also affects palms and soles but is distinguished by serology and systemic features.
Erythema multiforme minor
Correct. Three-zone target lesions on acral surfaces after herpes simplex, with skin involvement only.
Stevens-Johnson syndrome in its early phase
That would involve mucosal erosions in over 90% and epidermal detachment with a positive Nikolsky sign.
Acute urticaria with an unusual annular pattern
Wheals are migratory, blanch fully and each lasts under twenty-four hours without fixed targets.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 67-year-old man taking allopurinol for two weeks has fever, painful erythema and flaccid bullae, with sheets of epidermis separating over an estimated 45% of his body surface. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Toxic epidermal necrolysis

Correct — detachment above 30% with allopurinol exposure. The slide names allopurinol as the commonest cause IN ASIA, alongside aromatic anticonvulsants, sulfonamides, oxicam non-steroidals and nevirapine.
Stevens-Johnson and toxic epidermal necrolysis overlap
Overlap is defined by detachment between 10 and 30%.
Generalised bullous fixed drug eruption of the trunk
That produces discrete round plaques recurring at the same sites.
Autoimmune pemphigus vulgaris with widespread erosions
That evolves over weeks with intercellular immunoglobulin G on immunofluorescence.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 36-year-old woman with suspected dermatitis herpetiformis is to have a biopsy. Which specimen and test confirm the diagnosis?
opts: Serum sample for immunoglobulin A anti-endomysial antibody testing
Serology supports the diagnosis but is not the gold standard test.
Perilesional skin for direct immunofluorescence, seeking granular immunoglobulin A in the dermal papillae
Correct — this is the gold standard, and perilesional rather than lesional skin is the key detail.
Lesional skin for haematoxylin and eosin, seeking subepidermal blistering with neutrophils
Histology supports the diagnosis but immunofluorescence is what settles it.
Small bowel mucosa on endoscopy, seeking villous atrophy of the duodenum
That confirms coeliac disease rather than the skin diagnosis itself.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 27-year-old man is considering botulinum toxin for axillary hyperhidrosis. Which is the most appropriate counselling point?
opts: It permanently destroys the sweat glands in the treated area
That describes microwave thermolysis rather than botulinum toxin.
It carries a risk of compensatory sweating elsewhere in over 30%
That risk belongs to endoscopic thoracic sympathectomy.
It commonly causes dry mouth and urinary retention as side effects
Those are the anticholinergic effects of oral therapy.
It is effective for three to six months, so retreatment will be needed
Correct — setting that expectation is specifically named in the patient education.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 30-year-old woman has had polymorphous light eruption ruin the first weeks of every summer for four years. It is now February. Which is the most effective preventive strategy?
opts: Prophylactic narrowband ultraviolet B, three times weekly for five weeks in spring
Correct — it induces tolerance and is named as the most effective preventive strategy.
Hydroxychloroquine at 200 mg twice daily started at the first eruption
That is for refractory cases rather than the most effective prevention.
A short course of oral prednisolone taken at the onset of each episode
That treats a severe acute episode rather than preventing recurrence.
Moderate-potency topical corticosteroid applied to the areas each spring
Topical steroids treat the acute eruption; they do not induce tolerance.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 66-year-old woman has an actinic keratosis on the cheek that has become indurated, tender and has bled twice. Which is the most appropriate next step?
opts: Begin imiquimod 5% twice weekly for a sixteen-week course
Field therapy does not address a lesion suspicious for invasion.
Begin diclofenac 3% gel and reassess it in three months
That is for mild disease and would delay diagnosis here.
Biopsy the lesion to exclude invasive squamous cell carcinoma
Correct — induration, tenderness and bleeding are the concerning features named for progression.
Apply liquid nitrogen with two to three freeze-thaw cycles
Destroying a lesion with concerning features forfeits the diagnosis.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 47-year-old man with early photoaging asks what single measure will most reduce further damage. Which is the most appropriate counselling point?
opts: Annual laser resurfacing, since it is the most effective option for texture
Resurfacing treats existing change rather than preventing new damage.
Oral antioxidant supplements taken daily through the summer months
Supplements are not among the named interventions for photoaging.
Daily broad-spectrum sunscreen of SPF 30 or higher, applied as the last skincare step
Correct — it is the single most evidence-supported intervention, at about one teaspoon for face and neck.
Nightly topical retinoid, since it reverses the collagen loss already sustained
Retinoid improves established damage but photoprotection is what prevents progression.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 62-year-old woman on amiodarone develops photosensitivity, and the cardiologist cannot substitute the drug. Which is the most appropriate management?
opts: Oral antihistamines taken each morning through the summer months
Antihistamines address pruritus and do not prevent phototoxic injury.
Strict photoprotection with broad-spectrum SPF 50 and physical blockers
Correct — zinc oxide and titanium dioxide are named where the agent cannot be withdrawn.
Prophylactic narrowband ultraviolet B phototherapy given each spring
That is used for persistent light reaction and for polymorphous light eruption.
Oral hydroxychloroquine at 200 mg twice daily as a long-term measure
That is reserved for refractory polymorphous light eruption.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 35-year-old woman has a clinically typical polymorphous light eruption. Which investigation is described as mandatory before the diagnosis is accepted?
opts: Photopatch testing to a standard series of photoallergens
That is reserved for suspected photoallergic contact dermatitis.
A skin biopsy of a fresh papule taken within the first day
Biopsy is supportive rather than pathognomonic and is not mandatory.
An antinuclear antibody panel including anti-Ro and anti-La
Correct — lupus must be excluded because it can present identically.
A urine, stool and red-cell porphyrin screen sent together
That is ordered only where erythropoietic protoporphyria is suspected.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 32-year-old woman with idiopathic erythema nodosum has painful shins interfering with work. Infection has been excluded. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
opts: Rest, leg elevation, compression stockings and a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug
Correct — supportive care first, with potassium iodide effective for idiopathic and recurrent disease.
A prolonged course of oral antibiotics directed at streptococcal infection
There is no evidence of active infection to treat.
Long-term systemic corticosteroids continued for several months
A short course may be used once infection is excluded, but not as prolonged therapy.
Surgical excision of the most symptomatic nodules on each shin
The condition is a reaction pattern and resolves; excision has no role.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 41-year-old woman newly diagnosed with rosacea asks whether treatment will cure it. Which is the most appropriate counselling point?
opts: A twelve-week course of oral antibiotics usually produces a permanent remission with no need for any further treatment
Therapy controls symptoms; it does not eliminate the disease.
Avoiding alcohol alone will resolve the condition within several months
Alcohol is one trigger among many and avoidance does not cure it.
Laser treatment removes the underlying disease and prevents any recurrence
Laser addresses telangiectasias and erythema but not the underlying condition.
It is a chronic condition that therapy controls rather than eliminates, so long-term management and daily sun protection are expected
Correct, alongside a trigger diary and gentle non-irritating skincare.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 64-year-old woman has one facial pigmented macule that is asymmetric with an irregular border and two darker areas within it, unlike her other lesions. Which is the most appropriate next step?
opts: Begin topical hydroquinone 4% and review in three months
Bleaching an atypical pigmented lesion delays a melanoma diagnosis.
Reassure and arrange routine review in twelve months
The asymmetry and colour variation warrant assessment now.
Biopsy the lesion to exclude lentigo maligna
Correct — atypical or uncertain morphology on dermoscopy is the stated indication for biopsy.
Treat the lesion with cryotherapy for five seconds
Destroying an atypical lesion removes the ability to diagnose it.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 19-year-old man has extensive blistering sunburn over his back and chest with fever, nausea and tachycardia after a day on the water. Which is the most appropriate next step?
opts: Start oral antibiotics to prevent secondary infection of the blistered skin
Prophylactic antibiotics are not indicated for uninfected burn blisters.
Admit for intravenous fluids and wound care given the systemic toxicity
Correct — severe blistering above 20% of the body surface with systemic symptoms warrants hospitalisation.
Deroof the blisters in clinic and dress the base with a non-adherent layer
Intact blisters are protective and should not be popped.
Discharge with oral ibuprofen and aloe vera gel, reviewing in one week
That underestimates a presentation with fever, nausea and tachycardia.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 40-year-old woman with dermatitis herpetiformis is doing well on dapsone and asks whether she really needs to change her diet. Which is the most appropriate counselling point?
opts: Dapsone alone controls the condition completely, so a change in diet is optional provided the rash stays quiet
Dapsone gives rapid symptom relief but does not address the underlying enteropathy.
The diet is needed only if she develops gastrointestinal symptoms in the future
Nearly all patients have gluten-sensitive enteropathy even when gastrointestinally asymptomatic.
A reduced-gluten diet is sufficient provided she avoids obvious sources of wheat
The diet must be strict; partial restriction does not achieve control.
A strict lifelong gluten-free diet is the cornerstone and may allow dapsone to be reduced or stopped over one to two years
Correct, and hidden gluten in medications, sauces and cross-contamination should be discussed.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: The parents of a child with severe Herlitz junctional epidermolysis bullosa ask what support is available. Which is the most appropriate response?
opts: Early palliative care integration is appropriate, alongside genetics counselling and family support resources
Correct — goals-of-care discussion, pain optimisation and psychosocial support are all indicated in this subtype.
Gene therapy will cure the condition entirely once the child is old enough to be enrolled for treatment
The approved topical gene therapy is for dystrophic disease and is not curative.
The condition improves substantially through childhood with wound care alone
Junctional disease carries the highest mortality of the subtypes.
Genetic counselling is unnecessary since the condition arises sporadically
Counselling is described as mandatory for all families.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 30-year-old woman has had daily wheals for four months despite a standard dose of cetirizine. She is otherwise well. Which is the most appropriate next step in management?
opts: Begin omalizumab at 300 mg subcutaneously every four weeks
Right drug, wrong point: omalizumab is for refractory disease after antihistamine optimisation.
Begin cyclosporine with monitoring of blood pressure and renal function
Cyclosporine is reserved for refractory autoimmune urticaria.
Prescribe a five-day course of prednisone at 40 to 60 mg daily
Short steroid courses are used for severe acute urticaria rather than chronic disease.
Increase the non-sedating antihistamine to up to four times the standard dose
Correct — scheduled up-dosing is the next step before adding other agents.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 33-year-old woman with resolved phytophotodermatitis is distressed by persistent brown streaks on her arms. Which is the most appropriate counselling point?
opts: The pigmentation fades over months, and daily sunscreen prevents it darkening further
Correct — reassurance is first line, with hydroquinone or azelaic acid if it persists.
The pigmentation is permanent and only laser resurfacing will remove it
It fades over months without any procedural intervention.
The pigmentation indicates ongoing inflammation requiring potent steroids
The acute phase has resolved; the pigment is post-inflammatory.
The pigmentation signals a risk of melanoma at those sites in future
There is no malignant risk from phytophotodermatitis.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 58-year-old woman is admitted with toxic epidermal necrolysis. She has a known lymphoma, a heart rate of 132, detachment of 35% of her body surface, blood urea nitrogen of 34 mg/dL, bicarbonate of 17 mEq/L and glucose of 190 mg/dL. Which score should be calculated and what does it indicate?
opts: A SCORTEN of 7, indicating a predicted mortality of about 90%
Glucose of 190 mg/dL is below the 252 mg/dL threshold, so it does not score.
A SCORTEN of 6, indicating a predicted mortality of about 90%
Correct — age, malignancy, heart rate, detachment, urea and bicarbonate each score, and glucose is below threshold.
A SCORTEN of 4, indicating a predicted mortality of about 35%
That undercounts; six of the seven variables are above threshold here.
A SCORTEN of 2, indicating a predicted mortality of about 12%
That would apply to a far less severe presentation than this one.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 22-year-old woman with primary axillary hyperhidrosis has not improved with nightly aluminium chloride. Which is the most appropriate next step?
opts: Endoscopic thoracic sympathectomy to provide permanent relief
That is a last resort for palmar disease refractory to everything else, and carries compensatory sweating risk.
Microwave thermolysis to destroy the axillary glands permanently
That is third-line procedural therapy rather than the next step.
Reassurance that the condition is caused by anxiety and will settle
Anxiety exacerbates but does not cause primary hyperhidrosis.
Glycopyrronium 2.4% cloth applied once daily, or an oral anticholinergic
Correct — topical glycopyrronium is approved for axillary disease, with oral anticholinergics as second line.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 39-year-old woman with Crohn's disease has biopsy-supported pyoderma gangrenosum that continues to enlarge on high-dose prednisone. Which is the most appropriate next treatment?
opts: Omalizumab at 300 mg subcutaneously every four weeks
That is approved for refractory chronic urticaria.
Topical high-potency corticosteroid applied to the ulcer base
Topical agents are used at the wound edges for pain rather than as systemic control.
Infliximab at 5 mg/kg intravenously
Correct — it is approved for pyoderma gangrenosum in inflammatory bowel disease and is the biologic of choice.
Surgical debridement of the ulcer bed followed by grafting
Debridement worsens the ulcer through pathergy and is specifically avoided.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 70-year-old man has more than thirty confluent actinic keratoses across his scalp and forehead. Which is the most appropriate treatment approach?
opts: Observation with photographic monitoring and review in twelve months
Confluent disease at this density warrants treatment rather than observation.
Field-directed therapy, such as topical 5-fluorouracil or photodynamic therapy
Correct — field cancerization means the surrounding normal-looking skin also carries mutations.
Lesion-directed cryotherapy to each keratosis over several sessions
Cryotherapy is standard for isolated lesions but leaves the affected field untreated.
Shave excision with curettage and electrodessication of every lesion
That is a lesion-directed technique and is impractical at this number.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 17-year-old girl with acanthosis nigricans is embarrassed and has been scrubbing her neck daily, believing it is dirt. Which is the most appropriate counselling point?
opts: The change is caused by friction from clothing against the neck and will settle with softer, looser fabrics
Friction is not the mechanism; hyperinsulinaemia drives keratinocyte proliferation.
The change is permanent and no intervention will alter its appearance at all
Treating the underlying cause and losing weight both improve the findings.
The change indicates an underlying cancer in most adolescent patients
Malignant disease accounts for under 1% of cases and is rare at this age.
The change is a metabolic warning sign rather than a hygiene problem, and 5 to 10% weight loss improves it
Correct — the hygiene misconception is specifically addressed in the teaching.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 58-year-old man has hundreds of small papules over the trunk and limbs, present for a year and mildly itchy. Biopsy confirms granuloma annulare. Which is the most appropriate next step?
opts: Screen for diabetes, thyroid disease and dyslipidaemia, with age-appropriate malignancy screening
Correct — generalised disease in an adult over fifty carries these associations, including lymphoma.
Reassure that the condition is benign and arrange review in two years
That is appropriate for localised disease but generalised disease warrants systemic workup.
Begin intralesional triamcinolone to each of the affected lesions
Intralesional therapy suits symptomatic localised lesions, not hundreds of papules.
Begin oral terbinafine on the assumption of a widespread dermatophyte infection of the trunk and limbs
The biopsy has confirmed granuloma annulare, which is not fungal.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 9-year-old boy develops target lesions and oral erosions two weeks after a persistent cough and fever. Which test should be ordered to identify the trigger?
opts: Mycoplasma pneumoniae immunoglobulin M serology or polymerase chain reaction
Correct — elevated Mycoplasma immunoglobulin M is characteristic in children and atypical presentations.
Herpes simplex virus polymerase chain reaction from a skin swab
Herpes triggers most adult cases, but the respiratory prodrome here points elsewhere.
Antistreptolysin O titre with a throat culture for group A streptococcus
That combination investigates erythema nodosum instead.
Serum immunoglobulin A anti-tissue transglutaminase antibodies
That serology investigates dermatitis herpetiformis and coeliac disease.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 24-year-old man has target lesions on the palms, and the clinical picture is not clear-cut. A punch biopsy is taken with direct immunofluorescence. Which result would support erythema multiforme?
opts: Intercellular immunoglobulin G throughout the epidermal layer
That pattern indicates pemphigus.
Negative direct immunofluorescence with interface dermatitis on histology
Correct — negativity is what distinguishes it from pemphigoid and pemphigus.
Granular immunoglobulin A within the dermal papillae on immunofluorescence
That pattern is the gold standard for dermatitis herpetiformis.
Linear immunoglobulin G along the basement membrane zone
That pattern indicates bullous pemphigoid.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A 52-year-old woman with papulopustular rosacea has not improved on topical metronidazole after eight weeks. Skin scraping shows a heavy Demodex burden. Which is the most appropriate next treatment?
opts: Azelaic acid 15% gel applied twice daily
Effective for this subtype, but ivermectin specifically targets the demonstrated Demodex burden.
A high-potency topical corticosteroid applied twice daily
Topical steroids are a listed trigger and can worsen rosacea.
Ivermectin 1% cream
Correct — it is superior to metronidazole in Demodex-associated papulopustular disease.
Brimonidine 0.33% gel applied each morning
That is an alpha-adrenergic agonist for erythema rather than for papules and pustules.
